timing: retrospective specification of previously generated candidate

sourceFacts.fact: Children with proximal pelvic-girdle weakness may use their arms to assist rising.
The Gowers manoeuvre includes pushing on the thighs to raise the trunk.

nodes: hands and feet with hips raised
sequence: hands and feet with hips raised
invariants: Same clothed child and plausible four-limb pose at every step.
Movement explains proximal weakness compensation; it is not unique to Duchenne.
expectedLabels: The hands help lift the trunk when hip-girdle muscles are weak
layoutSpecification: A four-step left-to-right movement sequence of the SAME clothed young child in teal t-shirt and ochre shorts. Profile/three-quarter views keep body mechanics clear. Step1 child on hands and knees. Step2 feet planted with hips high, both hands on floor in bear stance. Step3 trunk partly raised, knees mostly extended, both hands pressing onto own thighs just above knees. Step4 child nearly standing, hands higher on own thighs near hips to push torso upright. No hands pressing shins in final step, no extra limbs, no furniture support. Numbered small labels '1', '2', '3', '4'. Gentle arrows between steps. Title 'Gowers manoeuvre'. Bottom 'The hands help lift the trunk when hip-girdle muscles are weak'. No claim unique to Duchenne.
forbiddenAnatomy: No claimed anatomical reconstruction, diagnostic image, histology or literal neuroanatomical pathway
No organ cutaways or invented internal spatial relationships
